name: AgentLens-Bench
description: A benchmark dataset of 1,815 fully-annotated coding agent trajectories across 47 SWE-bench Verified tasks and 8 model backends, with process-level quality annotations. The trajectories are model-generated execution traces over human-authored open-source repositories. Features include ground-truth Prefix Tree Acceptors (PTAs) constructed from merged successful trajectories, multi-dimensional quality scoring (coverage, coherence, workflow similarity, stage completeness), five-category waste detection (regression loops, blind retries, redundant steps, unnecessary exploration, cyclic patterns), quality tier classification (Ideal/Solid/Lucky), and divergence-point localization. This is the first coding agent benchmark providing process-level quality annotations rather than binary pass/fail labels.
citeAs: Priyam Sahoo, Gaurav Mittal, Xiaomin Li, Shengjie Ma, Benjamin Steenhoek, Pingping Lin, and Yu Hu. AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation. In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026. arXiv:2605.12925.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers the 47 of an initial 60 SWE-bench Verified tasks with enough passing trajectories to build a task-level PTA. It includes trajectories from 8 specific frontier LLM models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6; GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2-codex, GPT-5.3-codex; Gemini 2.5 Pro) run with the OpenHands agent scaffold only. Results may not generalize to other agent scaffolds (e.g., terminal-only agents, multi-agent systems), other programming languages (SWE-bench is Python-heavy), or other task domains beyond bug-fixing in open-source repositories. Quality annotations are computed against task-level PTAs merged from five passing trajectories per task, which may not capture all valid solution strategies. The dataset should not be used as a definitive quality ranking of the included models, as evaluation conditions may vary. The quality_score column includes a pass/fail outcome term (10 points for passing trajectories), so it should not be used on its own to measure how well process quality predicts the outcome; the paper's pass/fail evaluation uses a separate outcome-free combined score.
rai:dataBiases: Selection bias: tasks are drawn from SWE-bench, which overrepresents well-maintained Python open-source projects (Django, scikit-learn, matplotlib, etc.) and may not reflect the distribution of real-world software engineering tasks. Model selection bias: only frontier models available at the time of collection (early 2026) are included; results may not generalize to future or smaller models. Survivorship bias in ground truth: merged PTAs are built from successful trajectories only, so the ground truth inherently represents strategies that worked, potentially missing valid alternative approaches that happen to fail on SWE-bench's test suites.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: This dataset does not contain personally identifiable information (PII). All trajectories are machine-generated sequences of tool calls and code edits produced by LLM-based coding agents operating on public open-source repositories. No human subjects were involved in trajectory generation. The underlying SWE-bench task descriptions reference public GitHub issues and contributors, which are already publicly available.
rai:dataUseCases: Validated in the paper: (1) separating passing trajectories into Ideal, Solid, and Lucky tiers by process quality; (2) comparing the eight included model backends by process quality alongside pass rate, including robustness checks on shared tasks and leave-one-model-out references; (3) failure and waste analysis, such as the dominant waste categories and Lucky Pass mechanisms per model; (4) pass/fail separation by the outcome-free combined score (AUROC 0.766 on the 1,815 trajectories). The intent-stage labels behind the scores were validated against seven annotators (Fleiss' kappa 0.933). Not yet established: whether selecting training data by quality score improves fine-tuned agents (this needs a controlled fine-tuning study), use of the annotations as process-reward supervision, other agent scaffolds or programming languages, real-time monitoring, and production deployment decisions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables quality-aware training of coding agents, potentially producing agents that solve problems more efficiently with fewer wasted steps and tokens, reducing computational cost and environmental impact. Supports reproducible agent evaluation research. Risks: the waste detection methodology could theoretically be used to optimize agents for adversarial purposes (e.g., finding efficient paths to introduce vulnerabilities), though the dataset itself contains only benign bug-fixing trajectories on public open-source code. The quality tier labels should not be used to make claims about the absolute capability of specific commercial LLM products. Mitigations: the release contains only bug-fixing traces on public open-source code, and the documentation positions process scores as diagnostics that complement functional correctness, security review, and human judgment, not as an approval mechanism for deploying code.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Trajectory Collection
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Coding agent trajectories were collected by running 8 LLM backends on SWE-bench Verified tasks with the OpenHands agent scaffold, with about five attempts per model and task. The 1,815 released trajectories are those annotated against a task-level PTA; the five donor trajectories per task used to build that PTA are not included. Trajectories were recorded as structured sequences of tool calls (file reads, edits, terminal commands, searches) with full inputs, outputs, and metadata. Collection and all later processing were carried out by the authors, using the OpenHands scaffold and each model provider's API; pass/fail labels come from the SWE-bench Verified test harness. No crowdworkers were involved.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: PTA Construction and Merging
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Each trajectory was converted into a Prefix Tree Acceptor (PTA)—a state machine where each state is an intent-labeled agent action. For quality annotation, five passing trajectories per task (selected with seed=42) were merged into a task-level PTA using a state-equivalence cascade (content hash, file scope, line-range overlap, and terminal-command grouping). The released ground_truth/ PTAs merge all passing trajectories of each task. Merged PTAs encode the known-good solution strategies for a task.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: Quality Annotation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Each non-seed trajectory was matched against the merged PTA to compute quality metrics: coverage of the best-matching PTA path, structural F1, coherence (forward-progress ratio of the trajectory's intent-stage sequence), workflow similarity (intent-stage LCS ratio), stage completeness, and temporal profile alignment. The report score is quality_score = 0.25*coverage + 0.25*(100*coherence) + 0.18*(100*stage_completeness) + 0.12*(100*workflow_similarity) + 0.10*f1 + 0.10*O, rounded and clipped to 0-100, where O is 100 for passing and 0 for failing trajectories. The outcome term shifts every trajectory with the same outcome equally, so it does not change their relative order. Waste detection identified 5 categories of inefficiency (regression loops, blind retries, redundant steps, unnecessary exploration, cyclic patterns), all GT-aware—patterns present in the reference PTA were excluded. Quality tiers were assigned from quality_score: passing trajectories are Ideal (>=70), Solid (47-69), or Lucky (<47); failing trajectories are partial_fail (>=40) or off_track (<40).

distribution.name: github-repository
distribution.description: The AgentLens repository, which hosts the full AgentLens-Bench release under agentlens-bench/.

distribution.name: ground-truth-ptas
distribution.description: 47 task-level merged Prefix Tree Acceptors, one JSON file per task.

distribution.name: trajectory-ptas
distribution.description: 1,815 per-trajectory PTAs: each trajectory's intent-labeled state sequence, one JSON file per trajectory, grouped by task.

distribution.name: quality-reports
distribution.description: 1,815 per-trajectory quality reports from matching each trajectory against its task-level PTA: scores, waste instances, divergence points, and stage comparison, one JSON file per trajectory, grouped by task.

distribution.name: dataset_summary.json
distribution.description: Machine-readable dataset summary with configuration parameters, statistics, tier distribution, and curation table.

distribution.name: tasks.csv
distribution.description: Per-task metadata table with 47 rows: trajectory counts, ground-truth PTA size, and processing time.

distribution.name: tasks.parquet
distribution.description: Per-task metadata table in Parquet format (same content as tasks.csv).

distribution.name: trajectories.csv
distribution.description: Main annotation table with 1,815 rows and 40 columns: quality scores, waste detection, divergence analysis, and per-stage coverage for every trajectory.

distribution.name: trajectories.parquet
distribution.description: Main annotation table in Parquet format (same content as trajectories.csv).

distribution.name: curation_table.json
distribution.description: Quality-guided curation strategies showing how filtering by quality score improves trajectory set composition.

recordSet.name: tasks
recordSet.description: Per-task metadata: trajectory counts, ground-truth PTA structure, and processing statistics for each of the 47 SWE-bench tasks.

field.name: task_id
field.description: SWE-bench task identifier (e.g., 'django__django-10880').

field.name: n_trajectories
field.description: Total number of trajectories collected for this task.

field.name: n_passing
field.description: Number of trajectories that passed SWE-bench tests.

field.name: n_failing
field.description: Number of trajectories that failed SWE-bench tests.

field.name: n_donors
field.description: Number of passing trajectories used to construct the ground-truth PTA (always 5).

field.name: n_assessed
field.description: Number of non-seed trajectories assessed against the ground-truth PTA.

field.name: n_errors
field.description: Number of trajectories that produced errors during quality assessment.

field.name: merged_pta_states
field.description: Number of states in the merged ground-truth PTA for this task.

field.name: merged_pta_transitions
field.description: Number of transitions in the merged ground-truth PTA for this task.

field.name: elapsed_s
field.description: Processing time in seconds for PTA construction and quality assessment.

recordSet.name: trajectories
recordSet.description: Main annotation table with 40 quality dimensions for each of the 1,815 trajectories: identity, quality scores, per-stage coverage, waste detection, and divergence analysis.

field.name: task_id
field.description: SWE-bench task identifier.

field.name: model
field.description: Agent model name (e.g., 'opus-4.5', 'gpt-4.1', 'gemini-2.5-pro').

field.name: trajectory_id
field.description: Unique trajectory identifier.

field.name: passed
field.description: Whether the trajectory passed SWE-bench tests.

field.name: n_states
field.description: Number of states in the trajectory PTA.

field.name: quality_score
field.description: Report quality score (0-100): 0.25*coverage_percent + 0.25*(100*coherence_score) + 0.18*(100*stage_completeness) + 0.12*(100*workflow_similarity) + 0.10*f1_score + 0.10*O, rounded and clipped, where O is 100 if passed and 0 otherwise. Because of the outcome term, use this column for tiers and for comparisons within the same outcome, not as a pass/fail predictor; subtract 10 from passing rows for an outcome-free score.

field.name: quality_tier
field.description: Quality tier classification from quality_score. Passing trajectories: ideal (score>=70), solid (47<=score<70), lucky (score<47). Failing trajectories: partial_fail (score>=40) or off_track (score<40).

field.name: verdict
field.description: Five-level verdict predicted from the matching metrics: PASS, LIKELY PASS, UNCERTAIN, LIKELY FAIL, or FAIL.

field.name: coverage_percent
field.description: Percentage of the states on the best-matching ground-truth PTA path that this trajectory matched (0-100).

field.name: precision_percent
field.description: Percentage of candidate trajectory states that matched ground-truth states (0-100).

field.name: f1_score
field.description: Harmonic mean of coverage and precision (0-100).

field.name: coherence_score
field.description: Trajectory coherence (0-1), computed from the trajectory's own intent-stage sequence: the forward-progress ratio, penalized for backtracks and blind retries. Higher values indicate more consistent forward progress.

field.name: temporal_profile_score
field.description: Temporal profile similarity (0-1): one minus the mean Jensen-Shannon divergence between the trajectory's and the PTA's intent-stage distributions over the early, middle, and late thirds of the trajectory.

field.name: workflow_similarity
field.description: Stage-transition longest common subsequence ratio (0-1).

field.name: stage_completeness
field.description: Fraction of ground-truth stages covered (0-1).

field.name: bottleneck_coverage
field.description: Minimum per-stage coverage percentage (0-100). Identifies the weakest stage.

field.name: weighted_score
field.description: Stage-importance-weighted coverage score.

field.name: stage_coverage_E
field.description: Exploration stage coverage percentage (0-100).

field.name: stage_coverage_I
field.description: Implementation stage coverage percentage (0-100).

field.name: stage_coverage_V
field.description: Verification stage coverage percentage (0-100).

field.name: stage_coverage_O
field.description: Orchestration stage coverage percentage (0-100).

field.name: regression_loop_count
field.description: Number of Exploration→Implementation→Exploration regression patterns detected.

field.name: regression_loop_waste
field.description: Number of wasted steps attributed to regression loops.

field.name: blind_retry_count
field.description: Number of sequences of 3+ consecutive identical (tool, file, stage) actions.

field.name: blind_retry_waste
field.description: Number of wasted steps attributed to blind retries.

field.name: redundant_step_count
field.description: Number of file re-reads with no intervening edit.

field.name: redundant_step_waste
field.description: Number of wasted steps attributed to redundant steps.

field.name: unnecessary_exploration_count
field.description: Number of post-implementation exploration actions on non-ground-truth files.

field.name: unnecessary_exploration_waste
field.description: Number of wasted steps attributed to unnecessary exploration.

field.name: cyclic_pattern_count
field.description: Number of multi-step repeated subsequences detected.

field.name: cyclic_pattern_waste
field.description: Number of wasted steps attributed to cyclic patterns.

field.name: total_wasted_steps
field.description: Sum of all waste categories (regression + blind retry + redundant + unnecessary exploration + cyclic).

field.name: waste_severity
field.description: Waste ratio: total_wasted_steps / n_states (0-1).

field.name: wasted_input_tokens
field.description: Total input tokens consumed by wasted steps.

field.name: wasted_output_tokens
field.description: Total output tokens consumed by wasted steps.

field.name: divergence_step
field.description: Step number where the trajectory first diverges from the ground-truth PTA.

field.name: divergence_fraction
field.description: Divergence step as a fraction of total states (0-1). Lower values indicate earlier divergence.

field.name: stage_order_match
field.description: Whether the trajectory's stage ordering matches the ground-truth stage ordering.

field.name: failure_reasons
field.description: JSON-serialized list of failure reasons with severity levels.

field.name: strengths
field.description: JSON-serialized list of identified trajectory strengths.

recordSet.name: curation_strategies
recordSet.description: Quality-guided curation strategies showing how filtering trajectories by quality score improves the composition of training sets.

field.name: strategy
field.description: Name of the curation strategy (e.g., 'Random (all passing)', 'Top-50 by score').

field.name: k
field.description: Number of trajectories selected by this strategy.

field.name: ideal_pct
field.description: Percentage of selected trajectories classified as Ideal tier.

field.name: solid_pct
field.description: Percentage of selected trajectories classified as Solid tier.

field.name: lucky_pct
field.description: Percentage of selected trajectories classified as Lucky tier.

field.name: mean_coherence
field.description: Mean behavioral coherence score across selected trajectories.

field.name: mean_score
field.description: Mean quality score across selected trajectories.

field.name: min_score
field.description: Minimum quality score among selected trajectories.
